reason: Compared the complete source definition at lines 27-51, its conventions, and the following formalization remark against SM.polygonData and every component definition. Plane is the concrete real coordinate plane and LabelledTuple n is precisely a function ZMod n to that plane. Polygon requires n >= 3 and is the quotient by the equivalence relation Q = shift k P. shift 1 sends coordinate i to P(i+1), so these are exactly the cyclic orbits, with neither a distinguished vertex nor an additional geometric identification. No distinctness, genericity or nonzero-edge condition is imposed; coincident vertices and zero edges remain legal. edge and edgeSegment have the exact tail-indexed vector and closed affine-segment formulas. incident, adjacent (including self-adjacency), remote, remoteToVertex and remoteToVertexAndEdges reproduce the specified modular index sets exactly. The aggregate and its audited semantic dependencies include every one of these definitions, resolving the initial incomplete hash coverage. SM.sum_edges proves the source's zero-sum assertion for all nonzero n and therefore every source n >= 3. edge_shift, edgePoint_shift and edgeSegment_shift implement the induced index relabelling. Index-only incidence/remoteness formulas are unchanged by simultaneous translation, by cancellation in ZMod n. The source expressly permits working with labelled representatives and recording equivariance, so no quotient-valued fixed-index edge is required. This review covers this definition, not the later manifold assertion or any unimplemented construction.

Plane = ℝ×ℝ (l.13); LabelledTuple n = ZMod n → Plane (l.14) is (ℝ²)^n with indices in ℤ/n (label n ↔ residue 0, the relabelling the legend itself uses, immaterial since all clauses are shift/difference formulas); shift k P i = P(i+k) (l.22) so shift 1 is σ exactly as (σP)_i = μ_{i+1}; cyclicSetoid (l.33) relates P,Q iff Q = σ^k P, i.e. same orbit, and Polygon n (3 ≤ n) = Quotient of it (l.47) is (ℝ²)^n/(ℤ/n) with the source's n ≥ 3 carried as an argument; edge P i = P(i+1) − P i (l.49) is ℓ_i; edgeSegment (l.54) is {μ_i + tℓ_i : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1}; incident i j ↔ j ∈ {i−1,i} (l.60); adjacent i j ↔ j−i ∈ {−1,0,1} (l.63, reflexive as printed, consistent with the SM15 lem:g1(iv) gloss); remote = ¬adjacent (l.66); remoteToVertex = ¬incident (l.68); remoteToVertexAndEdges ↔ j ∉ {i−2,i−1,i,i+1} (l.70). No distinctness, nonzero-edge or genericity condition is imposed, matching the last sentence of the definition. The clause Σℓ_i = 0 is stated (and proved) as sum_edges (l.86) for all NeZero n, covering n ≥ 3. The aggregate polygonData (l.96) binds Polygon, shift, edge, edgeSegment and all five index relations; LabelledTuple/cyclicSetoid/edgePoint enter through them, and det/bracket (l.16–17) match the conventions of sec:conventions. Nothing is vacuous. The SM15 text is unchanged for this label, so the accepted statement matches SM15.
